manufacturer_data.description: Advertised names from the vendor app's scan config, in the groups it uses them: thermoproNames (Thermopro, TP901, TP902, TP922, TP939, TP938, P900, TP903, TP904, TP25, TP910, TP920, TP930, TP923, TP924), tempSpike (TP960R, TP962R, I61, TP970R, TP960W, I61W, TP971R/972R, TP963, TP971S/972S, TP973R, TP965R, TP966R), tp940 (TP940R), tempWifi (TP980R), infrared (P426, P925), plus the legacy SmartBBQ. "TempPro" and "iBBQ" are NOT advertised names. The prefixes above cover that set without enumerating every model; the app matches on the exact names.

device.name: ThermoPro TempSpike / TP9xx BBQ Thermometer
device.notes:
Extracted by static analysis of the official ThermoPro companion app.
Its BLE stack is the OEM's (Adsmart, the OEM behind ThermoPro's
connected devices), not ThermoPro-specific code.

TRANSPORT IS PLAIN BLE GATT — NOT BLE MESH. The app contains no mesh stack
(no/nordicsemi/android/ holds only ble/ + support/; no Mesh Proxy 0x1828,
no PB-GATT, no provisioning anywhere in the sources). Two independent RE
efforts agree: daniel-corbett/thermopro-cli calls it "a simple BLE
notification-based protocol", and Bluetooth-Devices/thermopro-ble decodes
TempSpike probes passively from advertisements with no connection at all.
An earlier revision of this spec describing BLE Mesh provisioning was
fabricated.

THERE IS NO SINGLE UNIVERSAL UUID SET. The app picks one of FIVE
per-family BLE configs at connect time — its BLE manager picks one of
five per-family config classes (16-bit codes expand to
0000XXXX-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB):
- TP9012 family (deviceType 7/8, its own per-family BLE config in the app): service
  0b863e05-ba64-4f7a-922d-007fd52dcaa9 — NOT 1086FFF0 — write FFF1,
  notify FFF2.
- TP922 (deviceType 22, its own per-family BLE config in the app): service
  baaafff0-0001-4e6e-886a-57d347c919fe, write BAAAFFF1-…, notify
  BAAAFFF2-….
- TP940 (deviceType 24) and TempSpike TP960 (deviceTypes 30/31):
  service 93bb7cab-eb14-c5a9-2354-a24f4df9330f with roles REVERSED —
  write = FF02, notify = FF01 — plus a read characteristic FF03.
- TP426 infrared (deviceType 50): service
  0f86fff0-63e8-4762-9dfb-7b6fe113376a, write FFF1, notify FFF2.
- Default (all other deviceTypes, incl. TP920/TP25W and TP980,
  the app's default BLE config): service 1086fff0-3343-4817-8bb2-b32206336ce8, write
  FFF1, notify FFF2.
Clients must identify the family (advertised name, per the app's scan
config)
before choosing a service; 1086FFF0 is the fallback, not the universal
case.

WRITE FRAMING IS PER-FAMILY. Only the TP9012 family wraps commands as
0xAA | payload | checksum | 0xFF, where checksum = sum of the payload
bytes EXCLUDING the opcode byte, & 0xFF (the app's TP9012 checksum helper);
its notifications mirror this with 0xAA at offset 0 and the opcode at
offset 1. TP920/TP25W-family frames have NO 0xAA/0xFF wrapper and a
trailing checksum that INCLUDES the opcode byte
(the app's TP920 checksum helper); this family additionally expects a
fixed init handshake write (starting 01 09 8a 7a ...) plus a
timestamp-sync command 0x28 after connect (thermopro-cli
create_handshake_command). TP940, TP960 (TempSpike) and TP980 send raw
opcode-prefixed frames with NO wrapper and NO checksum at all
(the app's TP940, TP960 and TP980 command builders emit the opcode
bytes as-is).

Eight device parser families are dispatched in the app (by its BLE
manager's notification callback): TP9012, TP920, TP940, TP960,
TP962, TP968, TP980 and TP426 (infrared). The TempSpike line
(TP960/962/968 and TP970-973) is the current retail focus.

TEMPSPIKE PASSIVE MODE: TP96x/TP97x probes broadcast probe index,
temperatures and battery voltage in BLE advertisement manufacturer data
(company id prepended LE by the parser) — fully decodable without
connecting (Bluetooth-Devices/thermopro-ble parser.py, actively
maintained). This is the cheapest integration path for those models and
obviates most of the setup below. TWO DIFFERENT LAYOUTS EXIST — an
earlier revision of this spec claimed "°F + 54 offset" for all of them,
which is wrong for TP96x:
- TP96x / TP970 (7-byte payload; a 13-byte variant appends 6 bytes —
  observed to be the reversed base-station MAC — which are ignored):
  "<BHHH" = probe_index u8, internal_temp u16, battery_voltage u16,
  ambient_temp u16. Temperatures are INTEGER values with a -30 offset
  (raw - 30), NOT °F (parser.py:184-206).
- TP97x (23-byte payload): "<BHHfffHHH" = probe_index u8, ambient_temp
  u16, battery_voltage u16, then three float32 internal temperatures
  (tip/center/end), three u16 ignored. Only THIS family encodes temps
  as float32 °F with a +54 offset: celsius = (raw - 54 - 32) * 5/9 —
  the same fahrenheit_to_celsius(x - 54) the connected TP980 path uses
  (parser.py:155-182).
Battery from advertisements uses a fitted tanh curve (mV → %):
52.317286 * tanh(v/273.624277936 - 8.76485439394) + 51.06925, clamped
0-100 (tp96_battery).

FIRMWARE/DFU: the app picks its updater by the app-internal deviceType
it assigned the unit, and only two deviceTypes are ever offered a BLE
update. deviceType 40 (the TP980R scan name, i.e. the TP980 variant)
gets the Silicon Labs Gecko OTA path (OTA service
1d14d6ee-fd63-4fa1-bfa4-8f47b42119f0, control
f7bf3564-fb6d-4e53-88a4-5e37e0326063, data
984227f3-34fc-4045-a5d0-2c581f81a153) with a bundled GBL image,
version 1.17. deviceType 22 (the TP920-family Wi-Fi units that report
type byte 0x62, scan names TP922/TP923/TP924, which are not a variant
of this spec) gets the ASR560X path (service
0917fe11-5d37-816d-8000-00805f9b34fb, write 09170001-…, notify
09170002-…) with a bundled ASR560X image, version 2.5, string
app-2.5.0-20251011.1000. TempSpike (TP960/TP962/TP968), TP940 and
TP9012 units are never offered an update, so the ASR560X image says
nothing about TempSpike silicon. The app also declares a 0x1850
service (0x2C00/0x2C01) in a DFU config that no GATT lookup ever
reads. Details are in the firmware_update feature.

ThermoPro is rebranding to "TempPro" (announced ~April 2026; temppro.com);
the app already references both buythermopro.com and temppro.com.

credentials.notes: No credential protects the BLE link itself — any central can connect and exchange commands. WiFi/cloud binding is NOT TP980-only: TP980 (scan name TP980R, the app's "tempWifi" group) uses notification opcodes decimal 80-84 = 0x50-0x54 (an earlier revision of this spec wrote "0x80-0x84", confusing decimal with hex) for wifi-scan/wifi-connect/wifi-check and cloud binding, returning the WiFi MAC, an 18-char device did and the bound-user field; the TP920/TP25W family has the same capability on opcodes 0x60-0x67 (writes: scan-wifi 0x60, connect-wifi 0x62, check-wifi 0x63, unbind 0x64, check-did 0x66; notifications: wifi-scan-return 0x61, wifi-connect-return 0x63/0x67, bound-notification 0x65, check-did-return 0x66 — from the app's TP920 command and parse code). Unlike the TP980 set, no decimal/hex confusion applies to these: the literals in the app are decimal 96-103, which equal hex 0x60-0x67 exactly as written here. The apparent write/notify overlaps are real request/response opcode sharing — the device's reply notification echoes the request's opcode (check-wifi write 0x63 → wifi-connect-return notify 0x63, check-did write 0x66 → check-did-return notify 0x66; 0x61 and 0x65 likewise double as the client's ack writes — the wifi-scan-return ack carrying the scan index, and the unbind ack), while 0x67 is a notification-only WiFi connect-state variant with no matching write. So a WiFi passphrase IS involved for those families, and TP980W is sold as a Wi-Fi model. No TP980 cloud broker endpoint is identifiable from static code; the binding rides the device did.
stored_on_device: WiFi families (TP980, TP920/TP25W): WiFi credentials + 18-char device id (did) / cloud binding

factory_reset.description:
`false` rather than `unknown`, but with low confidence, and the distinction is worth stating: the answer here is that the vendor documents no reset and the hardware exposes no control that could be one, not that a reset was found and ruled out. If a TempSpike ever turns out to have a service gesture, this should become `true`.
The pairing between the probe and its own transmitter is a separate matter from the BLE link this spec documents, and re-seating the probe in the transmitter is what re-establishes it.
factory_reset.effect: No factory reset is documented for the probe or its transmitter, and there is little for one to clear: the pair holds no credentials and no bond, and the probe is a sealed wireless unit that charges in its transmitter. Removing the probe from the transmitter and re-seating it is the only state change available.

methods.description: Scan for the advertised name (TP940R, TP980R, TP960R, Thermopro, SmartBBQ, ... per the app's scan config), identify the family from the name, connect to the family's service (see the five configs in device.notes — 1086FFF0-… is only the default for TP920/TP980 and others, write FFF1 / notify FFF2; TP940/TP960 use 93bb7cab-… with write FF02 / notify FF01; TP9012-family uses 0B863E05-…), enable notifications, and — on the TP920/TP25W/TP904 family — write the fixed handshake (01 09 8a 7a ...) plus timestamp sync (command 0x28) before issuing commands.

steps.action: Power the thermometer on; it advertises immediately.
Scan for the advertised name and identify the family; the service UUID in the device's own advertisement distinguishes it (1086FFF0 is the default, not the universal case).
Connect to the family's service, enable notifications on its notify characteristic, and send the family handshake where required.

Exchange commands in the family's framing (0xAA|payload|checksum|0xFF only on TP9012; checksum-including-opcode on TP920; raw opcodes on TP940/TP960/TP980) — or, on TempSpike models, just parse the advertisements.

setup.notes:
Plain BLE GATT: scan, identify the family (the UUID set and framing are per-family — see device.notes), connect, subscribe to the family's notify characteristic, run the short init handshake where the family requires it, then exchange opcode-prefixed commands. There is no provisioning, no pairing and no mesh layer. For TempSpike TP96x/TP97x models even the connection is optional — temperatures and battery arrive passively in advertisements.
Confidence is medium: the flows are read from the vendor app and two independent RE projects, but have not been run against a device here.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the thermometer to a BLE client: no keys, no pairing, no account. Switching controllers is scanning and connecting from the new one. (The WiFi families — TP980 and TP920/TP25W — additionally hold WiFi credentials and a vendor-cloud binding for their uplink — that binding is between the device and the cloud, not the BLE client.)

variants.description: Basic 2-probe BBQ thermometer (app code family — "TP9012" may be an internal/OEM designation; no retail page found)
variants.temperature_encoding_detail: (byteHigh << 4) + byteLow °C — the app's TP9012 probe-temperature decoder, NO /10. Sentinels: 0xFF,0x9C → -999.0; 0xDD,0xDD → -100.0; 0xEE,0xEE → 666.0

variants.description: 4-probe (+ambient slot) BBQ thermometer with meat temperature settings
variants.protocol_notes:
Per-probe push notifications (temperature-return opcodes 0x61/0x10,
probe index in byte 1) — there is NO polling state machine on this
family; the sequential per-probe target-temp flow belongs to TP980.
Other opcodes:
0x02 unit, 0x04 alarm setting, 0x05 alarm close, 0x06 device close,
0x67 color. Battery: raw×33 for both probes and box
(per the app's TP940 parser) — note this is the INVERSE of the
TP9012 formula (100 − 33×raw).
variants.temperature_encoding_detail: BCD: temp = (b1>>4)*100 + (b1&0x0F)*10 + (b2>>4) + (b2&0x0F)*0.1 °C; negative when the high nibble of b1 is 0x9 (subtract 1000). Disconnect sentinel 0xCC,0xCC → -999.0 (the app's TP940 probe-temperature decoder). The TP920/ TP25W family uses the same BCD digit layout but DIFFERENT sign/sentinel handling — sign = bit 0x80 of b1, sentinels 0xFF,0xFF → -999.0 / 0xDD,0xDD → -100.0 / 0xEE,0xEE → 666.0 (the app's TP920 probe-temperature decoder) — which is also the scheme thermopro-cli's decode_temperature implements, so the CLI is a valid reference for TP920 but NOT for TP940's sign/sentinels. TempSpike TP96x does not use BCD at all (u16 LE − 30, see the TP960 family below).

variants.description: TempSpike wireless single-probe spike + base station — the current retail focus (scan names TP960R, TP960W, I61, I61W)
variants.protocol_notes:
CONNECTED-MODE opcodes (spec previously had no TP96x GATT block despite
being named "tempspike"). Service 93bb7cab-…, write FF02 / notify FF01,
raw frames with NO checksum. Notifications (opcode at offset 0,
per the app's TP960 parser): 0x01 current temp, 0x02 history upload
first frame, 0x05 low battery upload, 0x06 box battery upload, 0x10
auto temp return, 0x11 low battery (alt), 0x12 probe connect upload,
0x13 temp alarm close, 0x14 ambient temp alarm close. Writes
(the app's TP960 command builder): 0x01 read temp, 0x02 read temp history, 0x03 auto-
notification on/off, 0x04 set probe temp alarm (°C and °F variants),
0x05 read battery state, 0x06 read battery (TP962), 0x15 set ambient
temperature alarm, 0x19 set temp unit, 0x1A read probe color. Battery:
u16 LE millivolt bands <2311 → 0%, 2311-2450 → 33%, 2451-2600 → 66%,
≥2601 → 100% (the app's TP960 battery decoder); passive ads use the
fitted tanh curve instead (see device.notes).
variants.temperature_encoding_detail: Connected mode: u16 LE minus 30 °C (temp = raw - 30) — the SAME encoding as the TP96x passive-advertisement layout, NOT the TP940 BCD scheme. Sentinels: 0xFF,0xFF → -999.9, and raw - 30 ≤ -30 → -999.9. Passive mode layout per TEMPSPIKE PASSIVE MODE in device.notes.

variants.description: TempSpike multi-probe variants (scan names TP962R, TP963, TP965R, TP966R)
variants.protocol_notes:
Same service/framing as TP960 but a WIDER notification dispatch
(per the app's TP962/TP968 parsers) adding a
sequential setTemp-probing state machine: 0x81 readNextProTemp,
0x04/0x84 setTempReturn, 0x06/0x16 box battery, 0x09/0x89 setUnitReturn,
plus 0x10 auto temp, 0x12 probe connect, 0x13/0x14 alarm close, 0x17
charge state change, 0x18 device close, 0x19 temp unit change, 0x1A
probe color check.
variants.temperature_encoding_detail: Same u16 LE − 30 °C encoding as TP960 (per the app's TP962/TP968 parsers); sentinel 0xFF,0xFF → -999.9.

variants.description: Pro-grade 4-probe thermometer with history upload and WiFi uplink (TP980/TP980W sold as Wi-Fi + Bluetooth models)
variants.protocol_notes:
History upload: multi-chunk transfer with a first frame (opcode 0x02)
and continuation frames, 6 bytes/record. Probe reading uses the
sequential per-probe target-temp / read-next-probe state machine
(the app's TP980 parser — an earlier revision of this spec
misattributed it to TP940). Notification opcodes: 0x11 temp
return, 0x12 probe connect, 0x13 temp alarm close, 0x14 ambient temp
alarm close, 0x17 charge state change, 0x18 device close, 0x19 temp
unit change, 0x1A probe color check, 0x20 temp auto-return, and
decimal 80-84 = 0x50-0x54 for WiFi scan/connect/check plus cloud
binding (did, bound-user). Battery: u16 LE millivolt bands <2311 → 0%,
2311-2450 → 33%, 2451-2600 → 66%, ≥2601 → 100%
(per the app's TP980 battery decoder).
variants.temperature_encoding_detail: IEEE 754 float32 read LITTLE-ENDIAN (Nordic Data.FORMAT_UINT32) at offsets 5/9/13 (in the TP980 temperature-return path). The wire value is °F with a +54 offset: convert as °C = (raw - 54 - 32) * 5/9 — the same fahrenheit_to_celsius(x - 54) the thermopro-ble parser applies for TP97x.

evidence.bundled_firmware: Two OTA images ship inside the app: an ASR560X image, version app-2.5.0-20251011.1000, and a Silicon Labs image, version 1.17.
reference_implementations: github.com/Bluetooth-Devices/thermopro-ble (passive advertisement parser used by Home Assistant)
evidence.static_analysis: Static analysis of the official ThermoPro companion app. Its OEM BLE stack is where the five per-family configs (UUID sets, framing), the scan-name table, the per-model command and parser classes, and the two OTA paths were read.

dfu_mode.notes: The app's scan filter includes the exact name "OTA". It accepts such an advertisement only at the address of a unit it has already bound, so the unit keeps its address in AppLoader. On reconnecting to a unit whose name is now "OTA", the app writes 0x00 to OTA Control again, streams the GBL to 984227f3-… in MTU-sized writes, then writes 0x03. On success it restores the stored name to TP980R and disconnects. A scanner that sees "OTA" at a known TP980 address has found that unit mid-update.

enter.notes: The app writes 0x00 to OTA Control (f7bf3564-…) on the running TP980, which reboots it into AppLoader. It offers this only when the unit's reported BLE firmware version is above 1.0 and below the bundled 1.17.

image.format: Silicon Labs GBL (the app's bundled image, version 1.17).
image.notes: The bundled GBL's header marks it encrypted and signed. It carries an encryption-init tag, encrypted program tags (AES-CTR) and a 64-byte ECDSA P-256 signature tag. Whether this unit's Gecko bootloader enforces the signature is a build option and is not established. Because the payload is encrypted, a replacement client can deliver the vendor's image but cannot build a new one without the device key. The image ships in the app and stays there.

dfu.notes: From static analysis of the vendor app (its per-deviceType OTA dispatch, OTA config and scan config) and of the bundled image's header, not run on hardware. The Silicon Labs OTA data characteristic 984227f3-… exists only in AppLoader on a stock stack, which is why only the OTA service is listed under `services`. `vendor_cloud`: when no BLE update applies, the app asks the ThermoPro cloud for this unit's firmware and, if an update is listed, sends a cloud IoT command (id 65503, payload 0xFF). The unit then fetches the update itself over Wi-Fi. What that updates (the Wi-Fi module or the whole unit) is not established. The app also declares a 0x1850 service (write 0x2C00, notify 0x2C01) in a DFU config that it instantiates but never looks up on a device. No mechanism is inferred from it.

characteristics.description: Client → device command channel. Framing is per-family: on TP920 frames carry a trailing checksum that INCLUDES the opcode (no 0xAA/0xFF wrapper); on TP980 frames are raw opcode bytes with no checksum. This is a custom vendor service — NOT the BLE Mesh Proxy service (that would be 0x1828); there is no mesh anywhere in this product.
